name: drops_small
description: The AP award (0x798a00), the reward-list add (0x798ac0) and the end-of-battle AP settle (0x798b70).

harness.note: the real machine code of the functions; only the battle RNG function is replaced by a script (rngDraws is what the game asked for)

notes: in.fn: rollDrops | rollGear | awardAp | rewardAdd | apSettle; in.args its plain arguments (rollDrops: killer id, overkill flag, status word).

in.loot: {gil, ap, apOk, ch [2 chance bytes], gear (gear chance), items/qty (4), oItems/oQty (4), bribe [item, factor], gf [slotBase, b2e, b2f, b30, abilityBase], rows {"type + 2 * owner": [8 u16]}}; only the ability row the roll used is kept, and the replay with the pruned record gave the identical result.

in.rec {id: [autoB, inBattle, dead, apBlocked]} for slots 0..0x11; victim {marker, value} (marker 2 = bribed); killerAeon {id: 0|1}; joined [party ids with the joined bit]; groups {a_ability record: group byte}; R {gil, ap {id: n}, items [[id, qty]], gear: entries already in the list}; g {ap100, gil100, hit, rare, mode, lang}.

out: gil, ap {id: n} (changes only), items + itemCount, gearCount, gear (the new entries as hex of their 22 bytes; the name word is a fixed stub value 0x1234 because the naming functions are cosmetic and replaced), bribeItem (+0x2a after the call).
awardAp: chr [autoB, inBattle, dead, apBlocked], total; out {ret, total}. rewardAdd: R.items. apSettle: rows {id: [acted, inBattle, dead, stoned, ap, backup, battles]}, tail; out {ap, stat0, tail}.
